_READ_THIS_FIRST.you_are: An automation agent (Astra, Grok, a browser runner, or a human) working Yasir A. Malik's job search.
_READ_THIS_FIRST.the_job: Take roles from automation/queue/pending/ to automation/queue/submitted/ or automation/queue/skipped/. Everything before that step is already automated and running.
rules: 1. NEVER put credentials, cookies, session tokens, or API keys in this repository. It is public and git history is permanent. Credentials live only on Yasir's own machine, in automation/runner/sessions/, which is gitignored.

2. NEVER answer immigration or work-authorization questions, salary HISTORY questions, demographic/EEO questions, or anything requiring a signature or attestation. Stop and move the role to skipped/ with the blocking field named in agent.notes.
3. NEVER send email as Yasir. Draft only. Approval for one message is never approval for the next.
4. NEVER substitute a different resume than package.resume. The selection rule lives in scripts/discover_jobs.py and exists so the document matches the role.
5. NEVER write 'OCC'. The examiner history is the Florida Office of Financial Regulation, 'alongside federal banking regulators' if context is needed.
6. NEVER write 'Dr. Malik' or 'CIA certified'. The DBA is in progress (expected 2028); the CIA is in progress, not held.
7. NEVER claim the dissertation is IRB-approved. IRB-25-0462 covers the COMPLETED anchoring-bias qualifying study only.
8. Claim a role before acting on it (status: claimed) and commit, so two runners cannot submit the same application twice.
9. A submission with no employer confirmation email did not happen. confirmation_ref must point at real evidence.
10. Work highest score first; among equal scores prefer sponsor_employer: true. Sponsorship is the ranking constraint on this search, not a nice-to-have.

11. NEVER state a career-length number - '20 years', '15+ years', 'two decades', 'a decade'. Owner's rule, 12 Sep 2026: it dates him. Name the institutions instead (Citi, JPMorgan Chase, Florida OFR). Employer-specific spans ('six years at JPMorgan') are fine - those describe a job, not an age.
